text: {"summary":"Recommend the two-number scheme: state a target (~500 characters) plus a strictly lower generation budget (~600) as a self-check ceiling, keeping the 1200-character hard acceptance ceiling unchanged and unmentioned as a target; fix via prompt guidance plus a single validation-triggered reprompt, not CLI token clamps.","payload":{"vote":"two_number_scheme","confidence":"medium-high","recommendation":{"target_chars":500,"generation_budget_chars":600,"hard_acceptance_ceiling_chars":1200,"ceiling_unchanged":true,"budget_is_soft_prompt_level_only":true},"suggested_prompt_language":"Write the rationale as prose of about 500 characters. Do not exceed 600 characters. If you are nearing that budget, finish the current sentence and stop rather than continuing; a shorter complete rationale is always preferred over a longer one. Never emit a truncated or mid-sentence rationale.","analysis":{"a_headroom":"A ~600 generation budget leaves ~600 characters (2x) of slack against the 1200 hard ceiling, which comfortably absorbs normal verbosity variance and makes first-call compliance the expected case rather than a coin flip.","b_truncation_confusion":"Real but low and mitigable. The confusion mode comes from presenting two numbers as competing ceilings; presenting one as the aim and one as the do-not-exceed self-check, with an explicit 'finish the sentence, prefer shorter, never truncate mid-sentence' clause, resolves the ambiguity. The budget is prompt-level guidance only and is never enforced by the parser, so overshoot below 1200 remains a pass, not a failure.","c_root_cause":"Consistent with the V3/V4 evidence but not proven by it. Stating a single number equal to the acceptance ceiling makes that number function as an anchor/target rather than a limit, and leaves zero slack for verbosity variance, so any overshoot is an immediate hard failure. Two independent seat-anthropic failures on non-retried first calls fit that pattern. Recommend logging observed rationale lengths in the next exercise to confirm the anchoring hypothesis rather than treating it as settled.","d_provider_neutrality":"Preserved. The guidance is plain natural-language prose with no vendor-specific parameters, tokenizer assumptions, or schema features, so seat-anthropic, seat-openai, and seat-google receive a byte-identical instruction. Character counts (not tokens) keep the instruction tokenizer-agnostic. Per-seat tuning of the numbers would break provider neutrality and should be avoided.","e_cli_constraints":"Prompt-level generation budget alone is the right first step; do not add CLI-level structured-output or max-token constraints in this change. A hard token cap converts a soft overshoot into a mid-sentence truncation and likely invalid JSON, which is a worse failure than the current one on constrained token budgets. If the budget instruction proves insufficient, the correct escalation is a single validation-triggered reprompt ('your rationale was N characters; rewrite it under 500') rather than decoder-level clamps, because a reprompt preserves well-formed output."},"scope_guardrails":["Hard acceptance ceiling of 1200 characters / 4096 UTF-8 bytes stays enforced in the parser/builder and is untouched.","Change is confined to the reviewer prompt packet text; no change to ADR-0005 quorum semantics, DecisionRecord.recordHash, or any authorization/execution boundary.","Advisory evidence only; zero effect on quorum."],"residual_risks":["Model may still anchor on the 600 figure and consistently produce ~600-character rationales; acceptable, since that is half the hard ceiling.","Two numbers add prompt surface that must be kept consistent if the ceiling is ever revised; mitigate by deriving the documented numbers from the ceiling constant in the packet template rather than hardcoding them in prose in multiple places."],"followups":["Instrument the next exercise to record per-seat rationale character counts so the anchoring hypothesis in (c) is confirmed or falsified with data.","Add one bounded retry on CHARACTER_LIMIT before failing ASSESSMENT_VALIDATION, so a single overshoot does not sink the exercise."]}}
